categories.name: Documents & Tech
items: Boarding passes (WN #3914 + WN #1324)
Driver's license / ID
Credit cards + cash for farmers markets
Phone charger + portable battery pack
Car charger
Earphones for daughter on flights
Download offline maps for Colorado before leaving

categories.name: Clothing
items: Layers for Pikes Peak summit (30°F cooler than base)
Layers for Maroon Bells (9,580 ft — can be cold even in June)
Rain jacket / windbreaker (afternoon thunderstorms)
Comfortable hiking shoes (all 3 family members)
Swimsuit x3 (rafting + hot springs + main pool)
Water shoes / sandals for pool + river
Casual clothes for Aspen/Vail village walking
Warm fleece or light jacket for evenings at altitude

categories.name: Hiking & Outdoors
items: Sunscreen SPF 50+ (altitude sun is intense — apply on TOP of legs/arms for rafting)
Sunglasses + hat (UV stronger at altitude)
Reusable water bottles x3 (hydration critical — altitude dehydrates fast)
Small daypack for Maroon Bells trail
Trail snacks for Maroon Bells (café is overpriced)
Trekking poles (optional — helpful on Crater Lake Trail)
Insect repellent

categories.name: Health & Altitude
items: Altitude: start hydrating on the plane — drink double usual water
Ibuprofen / Tylenol (altitude headaches common Days 1-3)
Consider Diamox if altitude sickness history (consult doctor)
Avoid alcohol first 48 hours at altitude
Hand sanitizer
Band-aids + blister pads (new hiking shoes + trails)
Motion sickness tablets (Independence Pass switchbacks if taking that route)

categories.name: Daughter's Bag
items: Snacks for long drive days
Activity book / tablet for I-70 stretches
Earphones
Small backpack for trail days
Camera or use phone for her own photos
Cash for farmers market treasures (Vail)

categories.name: Car Essentials
items: Download offline Google Maps before leaving
Check cotrip.org morning of Day 6 if taking Independence Pass
Confirm rental car is full-size SUV (luggage + mountain roads)
Car phone mount for navigation
Snacks + drinks for drive days
